title: ERC-7540 Async-Vault Request Accounting
description: Recomputes ERC-7540 asynchronous-vault request accounting from caller-declared request state. ERC-7540 extends ERC-4626 with a three-state request lifecycle used by funds that cannot settle a deposit or redemption in the same transaction: an amount is Pending after a request, becomes Claimable when the vault fulfils it, and is Claimed when the holder calls deposit, mint, withdraw or redeem. This tool applies a sequence of claims against the claimable buckets at the pro-rata rate they were made claimable at, tracks the pending, claimable and claimed split for both legs, reports the rounding residue a sequence of partial claims strands, and checks the standard's invariants by name. ERC-7540 mandates no rounding direction for a partial claim, so the direction is a declared parameter and the opposite direction's result is reported beside it. Never reads any chain: it cannot know whether the declared amounts match a deployed vault, when a pending request will be fulfilled, whether the controller is authorised, or whether a claim transaction would succeed.

request_id.description: Non-negative integer as a decimal or 0x-hex string, default '0'. Zero is the standard's aggregate convention, where the vault discriminates purely by controller and amounts across requests are fungible; a non-zero id is a discrete request that must stay at one pro-rata rate.

deposit.description: Deposit leg: {pending_assets, claimable_assets, claimable_shares}. The two claimable fields are a pair fixing the rate the vault made the request claimable at, so they must be both zero or both non-zero.

redeem.description: Redeem leg: {pending_shares, claimable_shares, claimable_assets}. Same pairing rule as the deposit leg.

claims.description: Claims to apply in order. Each entry is {leg, unit, amount}: leg is 'deposit' or 'redeem'; unit is 'requested' (deposit: assets, redeem: shares) or 'received' (deposit: shares, redeem: assets), matching the standard's four claim overloads.

claim_rounding.description: 'down' (default) or 'up'. ERC-7540 mandates NO direction for a partial claim, so one must be declared. Every claim reports what the other direction would have produced.

chain_id.description: Optional free-text label carried through to the receipt for the reader's own record-keeping. Never a selector: no branch in this tool reads it and no result depends on it.

network_label.description: Optional free-text network label, carried through verbatim. Never a selector.

mcp_tool_definition.name: recompute_erc7540_request_accounting
mcp_tool_definition.description: Recomputes ERC-7540 asynchronous-vault pending/claimable/claimed request accounting from declared state, applies a claim sequence at the bucket's pro-rata rate under a declared rounding direction, and reports the standard's invariants by name.

dust.note: A stranded amount is one side of a claimable bucket left non-zero after the other side reached zero, so no further claim against it can be computed at the bucket's rate.

invariants.name: pending_and_claimable_disjoint
invariants.source: ERC-7540: pendingDepositRequest/claimableDepositRequest (and the redeem pair) each exclude the other state's amount.
invariants.detail: Structural: this kernel models pending and claimable as separate buckets and never moves an amount between them, so the two views can never double-count. A claim only ever draws from the claimable bucket.

invariants.name: claim_never_skips_claimable_state
invariants.source: ERC-7540: "Requests MUST NOT skip or otherwise short-circuit the Claim state."
invariants.detail: Every claim drew only from an amount already in the Claimable state.

invariants.name: claim_within_claimable_bounds
invariants.source: ERC-7540 max* views track the claimable amount (the standard notes maxDeposit moves in sync with claimableDepositRequest).
invariants.detail: No claim exceeded its leg's remaining claimable amount.

invariants.name: single_prorata_rate_for_nonzero_request_id
invariants.source: ERC-7540: "If a Request with requestId != 0 becomes partially claimable, all requests of the same requestId MUST become claimable at the same pro-rata rate."
invariants.detail: Not applicable: request_id is 0, the aggregate-by-controller convention, where amounts from separate requests are fungible and no single per-request rate is asserted.

invariants.name: partial_claim_rounding_direction_is_declared_not_mandated
invariants.source: ERC-7540 states no rounding direction for a partial claim. ERC-4626 fixes a direction per function; ERC-7540 does not extend that to claims.
invariants.detail: Direction "down" was supplied by the caller, not derived from the standard. Each claim reports what the opposite direction would have produced.

output_example.note: Recomputes ERC-7540 asynchronous-vault request accounting from caller-declared request state: applies a sequence of claims against the claimable buckets at the implied pro-rata rate, tracks the pending/claimable/claimed split, and checks the standard's stated invariants (pending and claimable are disjoint views; a claim never skips the Claim state; a non-zero requestId stays at one pro-rata rate). ERC-7540 mandates NO rounding direction for a partial claim, so the direction here is a declared parameter and the result of the opposite direction is reported alongside it. This kernel does NOT read any chain: it cannot know whether the declared amounts match any deployed vault, when or whether a pending request will be fulfilled (the standard leaves that timing unspecified), whether the controller is authorised, or whether a claim transaction would succeed.
